ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 and FATF Recommendation 12; all directors, shareholders and beneficial owners must be screened against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit domestic designation lists, United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List (UNSCR 1267/1988/2231), OFAC SDN List, EU and Australian DFAT consolidated sanctions lists, and adverse media and global PEP databases. Given the Class III medical device designation and laser micro-machining dual-use exposure, additional end-user, export-control and anti-counterfeit screening is required under the International Companies Regulations 1998 and applicable origin-jurisdiction export control law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry, Offshore Companies Section, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - International Company Name Approval administered through Licensed International Company Agents; MCIL online name-search portal and agent-mediated clearance channel
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in the Latin alphabet and in the English language; no local script or Samoan transliteration is required. The name must be distinguishable from names of existing domestic and international companies registered in Samoa and from registered trademarks. Romanized corporate suffixes only.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the licensed International Company Agent may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days from the date of the rejection notice. If the Registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 days from the notice of affirmation. Further recourse lies by way of judicial review proceedings in the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicature Act 1961. A resubmission of an alternative name incurs a new name search fee, and any approved name reservation may be renewed for a further 90-day period upon payment of the applicable extension fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office in Samoa is mandatory and must be maintained at the premises of the licensed International Company Agent; a purely virtual or mailbox-based office is not acceptable as the statutory registered office. The registered office serves as the legal seat for service of process and statutory notices. The actual Class III medical device manufacturing operations and warehousing must remain outside Samoa, as an International Company cannot carry on business with Samoan residents or hold Samoan land; commercial substance for tax and regulatory purposes resides in the offshore manufacturing and distribution chain.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-trivial for the MedTech high-risk tier; estimated at 5% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months. The Registrar of International Companies and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit may conduct on-site AML/CFT inspections of the licensed International Company Agent, and any non-compliance by the registered office in maintaining records may trigger inspection at the agent premises. There is negligible likelihood of inspection of offshore manufacturing facilities located outside Samoa.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), Part II (sections 6–12) incorporating an International Company; International Companies Regulations 2007
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association of an International Company (Form IC-02)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed; one (1) issued ordinary share is sufficient. Subscriber funds may be held under escrow only if expressly agreed with the licensed registered agent; no mandatory escrow account is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers to the Memorandum of Association hereby subscribe to the initial share capital of this International Company, and that the number, class and par value of shares issued to the initial subscriber be accepted and recorded in the share register. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office at the address of the licensed registered agent is adopted as the Company's statutory registered office, and that the registered office agreement be kept in the statutory records. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the following persons be and are hereby appointed as directors, secretary and officers: [insert names]. All officers are jointly authorised to open bank accounts, execute founding documents and complete all regulatory filings required to obtain industrial and environmental licences.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Name Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name reservation application through the SIFA online portal or physically at the Registrar's office. Provide the proposed company name and confirm acceptability, non-confusion and non-prohibited status. The name must end with the words 'International Company' or the abbreviation 'I.C.'.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form (IC-01)
Proposed Memorandum and Articles of Association draft
Consent of the proposed registered agent
Copy of the applicant's passport or identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, resubmit a revised name reservation with alternative names; no fee is refunded, but a new application may be filed immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Registry Office or Authorized Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, execute them before a notary public, and arrange for the signatures of the subscriber, directors and secretary to be witnessed. The registered agent must countersign to confirm acceptance of the registered office appointment.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notarized consent to act of each director and secretary
Written consent of the Samoa-licensed registered agent
Registered office address confirmation form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries notarization, have the original wet-ink documents re-verified by the notary and file a corrective affidavit within 14 calendar days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation package, including the executed Memorandum and Articles, all consents and the registered office agreement, together with payment of the official fees, using Form IC-02. Retain a receipted acknowledgment as evidence of filing.
required_dossiers: Form IC-02 statutory incorporation application
Original executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notarized signatures of all founding persons
Certificate of registered office and licensed agent
Consent of directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or notice to cure, file the corrected documents and clarifications within 7 business days; if an application lapses, re-file with a fresh fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Tax Exemption Endorsement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies and Ministry of Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: On approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the Company's corporate records are registered. The Company may apply for the International Company tax exemption certificate under section 120 of the Act to confirm tax-exempt status in Samoa.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by SIFA
Copy of the registered agent's certificate
Initial share register record
Tax exemption application (Form IC-05)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax exemption certificate is delayed, submit a written clarificatory statement to the Ministry of Revenue and request an expedited review; statutory remedies include mandamus.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Establishment of Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, adopt the board resolutions, record the minutes, issue share certificates, and open the corporate bank account. Ensure that the statutory registers including shareholders, directors, officers and charges are established and kept at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Board resolution minutes approving subscription and appointments
Share register and share certificates
Register of directors and officers
Registered office agreement
Corporate bank account documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any statutory record is rejected by the Registry, amend the record and file an explanatory memorandum with the Registrar; no enforcement action is taken during the cure period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa Medicines and Medical Devices Authority, Ministry of Health
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing Establishment Licence (Class III) for Drug-Eluting Coronary Stents

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) – Environment Assessment and Pollution Control Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 1 – Full EIA Report required for Class III medical device manufacturing involving polymer processing, laser micro-machining and solvent-based drug coating.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge: pH 6–9, BOD not to exceed 50 mg/L, TSS not to exceed 100 mg/L; VOC emissions must remain within Samoa's Ambient Air Quality Standard; all hazardous waste, including cytotoxic drug residue, must be licensed for storage and export under the Basel Convention permit regime.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority covering premises and chemical storage; structural load inspection certificate from Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure; occupational health and safety clearance for laser and cleanroom operations from the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) – Online services via the SRA Taxpayer Portal (sra.gov.ws)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must submit a TIN registration application using prescribed SRA Form (TF-01) with certified constitutional documents, director/beneficial owner due diligence, and a Samoa-registered registered office address. Once verified, SRA issues a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or VAT identification number for VAGST purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: International Companies (ICs) are exempt from Samoa income tax under the International Companies Act 1987; there is no general check-the-box election. An IC may elect to become a tax resident in rare circumstances, but such election negates the offshore-exempt status and is generally inadvisable for non-resident owners. No applicable hybrid-mismatch election exists for ICs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WS$100,000 taxable supplies per 12-month rolling period; voluntary registration permitted below threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time e-invoicing or fiscal clearance mandate currently applies; VAGST-registered persons must issue tax invoices (paper or digital PDF) showing the TIN/VAGST ID and tax amount, and retain records for SRA electronic-format inspections.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the supply of goods physically exported from Samoa within 28 days of supply, dental/medical goods supplied overseas, and certain internationally connected services. The exporter must hold documentary evidence of dispatch and receipt, and the goods must be exported to a foreign destination for a consideration paid in foreign currency.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SRA and Samoa Customs Service jointly scrutinize export zero-rating claims. Fraudulent or ineligible claims attract clawback of the unpaid VAGST, statutory interest, penalties up to 200% of the tax shortfall, fines up to WS$100,000, and potential imprisonment for directors/officers under the Tax Administration Act 2012 and the Criminal Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Falefa, Apia, acting as the Exchange Control Authority under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1977; the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) co-supervises the International Company (IC) registry and economic-substance filings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is managed under a controlled float against a trade-weighted basket dominated by USD, AUD and NZD. Current-account payments for goods and services flow freely through CBS-licensed authorized dealers, while capital-account transfers require documented CBS exchange-control approval. Resident companies face profit-remittance hurdles including WST surrender obligations and tax-clearance certificates. The International Company is statutorily non-resident, is prohibited from carrying on business with Samoan residents, and must transact exclusively in foreign currency (normally USD). Consequently, USD dividend and capital remittances to non-resident shareholders are freely executable after a CBS exchange-control notification, subject only to the IC's AML/KYC standing with its licensed bank and the absence of any WST-denominated local funding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident exporters must repatriate export proceeds to a licensed Samoan bank and offer the WST equivalent to an authorized dealer; CBS administrative guidance requires surrender within 90 days of shipment for goods on the Samoan export schedule. The International Company is exempt from the surrender regime: 100% of USD export receipts may be retained in the IC's designated USD clearing account at a CBS-licensed bank or held offshore, provided no conversion into WST occurs and no Samoan resident is a counterparty to the underlying transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operational Account plus Commercial Letter of Credit Issuance and USD Clearing Corridor via New York correspondent
Capital Escrow Account and secondary USD Operational Account
Secondary Operational Account limited to local regulatory deposits
Legacy IC accounts only; portfolio under transfer to BSP Samoa, new-to-bank onboarding suspended

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium restricted supporting role. Samoa maintains no fintech EMI or virtual-banking license; CBS does not recognize foreign EMI authorizations for holding WST or accessing local clearing. Global digital payment providers such as Airwallex, Currenxie or Wise may be used solely as non-routed pass-through vehicles for small supplier prepayments backed by a correspondent relationship with a CBS-licensed bank. Such EMIs cannot issue, advise, confirm or settle commercial letters of credit, cannot open Samoan resident accounts, and are not accepted as a primary clearing rail for Class III MedTech trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical mandate applies: at least one director or a CBS-approved authorized signatory must attend an in-person KYC interview at the bank's Apia branch. A general power of attorney executed in favor of a licensed Samoan attorney or a resident director satisfies the attendance requirement. Remote video KYC is acceptable only for secondary signatories when the IC is introduced by a licensed International Corporate Service Provider and apostilled incorporation documents are produced. The Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended) obliges banks to verify beneficial ownership through face-to-face or board-approved equivalent video verification before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-Risk Merchant Category: Class III drug-eluting coronary stent manufacturer combining a medical device with a pharmaceutical agent, triggering mandatory Enhanced Due Diligence under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit red-flag guidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISO 13485:2016 certificate; EU CE Mark under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 or US FDA Premarket Approval number specific to the drug-eluting stent; Samoa Ministry of Health importation/manufacturing notification; two years of audited financial statements; pharmacological dossier confirming the anti-restenosis drug substance and elution mechanism.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident offshore structure: 100% foreign-owned International Company with nominee directors and no Samoan economic footprint, presenting shell-company indicia.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Samoa International Finance Authority; certified register of directors, members and charges; beneficial ownership declaration identifying every ultimate natural person; legal opinion from licensed Samoan counsel confirming non-resident tax-exempt status; group organizational chart evidencing the operational manufacturing chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned and dual-use exposure: raw materials for stent manufacturing (nitinol tubing, bioresorbable polymers, taxol/everolimus-based drug compounds) sourced from the US, EU or China, triggering OFAC/EU sanctions screening on the full counterparty chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-Use Attestation signed by the ultimate hospital distributor; import certificate from the purchaser's national drug regulatory authority; supplier list pre-screened against OFAC and EU consolidated sanctions lists; customs declarations and airway/bill of lading for each consignment; contractual prohibition on resale to UN-sanctioned, OFAC-listed or EU-designated parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid in-out wire activity: high-velocity SWIFT MT103 flows and LC drawdowns without local payroll, rent or fixed-asset activity, characteristic of a money-velocity shell.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy and 12-month cash-flow waterfall; master raw-material supply agreements and stent offtake agreements; invoice-level reconciliation of every USD wire to the corresponding letter of credit or proforma invoice; quarterly independent auditor confirmation of deployed funds against capital expenditure and purchase orders.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for initial equity injection: SWIFT MT103 transfer from the parent shareholder's corporate account, normally a Singapore or Hong Kong treasury entity, directed to the IC's USD account at the CBS-licensed Samoan bank. Purpose code must be entered as equity contribution with descriptive reference 'Equity injection - WS_IC capital account' and, where the correspondent bank demands an ISO 20022 purpose code, use the cross-border investment classification. Supporting verification bundle: board resolution authorizing share allotment, updated register of members, remitting shareholder's bank statement evidencing source of funds, CBS Exchange Control declaration confirming the proceeds remain in USD with no on-lending to Samoan residents, and a sanctions-screening pass by the receiving authorized dealer. Foreign-source funds require no CBS monetary allowance or license, only notification where conversion to WST is contemplated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) commercial letters of credit - irrevocable LC (SWIFT MT700) issued by the Samoan issuing bank at the IC's request for raw-material and capital-equipment imports (nitinol tube, polymer coating, drug substance, laser micro-machining systems), advised through the beneficiary's bank, with settlement by SWIFT MT740 reimbursement or MT202 at 90-180 days usance; (2) SWIFT MT103 direct transfers for prepayments and balances below USD 250,000, supported by invoice, packing list and bill of lading; (3) for urgent high-value settlement, MT202 COV with full beneficiary ownership details. Samoa lacks domestic RTGS for USD, so value is credited through the bank's offshore USD correspondent (New York or Frankfurt), adding a one-to-two business-day clearing leg.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/WST forward contracts executed with a CBS-licensed authorized dealer (BSP or ANZ Samoa) for a maximum tenor of 12 months, restricted to the IC's documented WST-denominated trade exposure and declared to the CBS Exchange Control Division.

Offshore USD/WST nondeliverable forwards (NDF) transacted through Singapore or Hong Kong dealers solely to hedge genuine WST receivables or payables arising from permitted non-resident counterparties; settlement must occur in USD and cannot create a WST account in Samoa.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST) with non-resident banks, permissible only upon CBS prior approval and only where a valid non-resident WST exposure exists; practically unavailable to the IC because the International Companies Act prohibits WST business with Samoan residents.
EUR/USD and USD/CNH forwards or vanilla FX options hedging European and Chinese distribution and procurement flows, freely permissible without CBS approval since no WST leg is involved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual return of the International Company confirming authorized capital, shares, directors, members, registered office, and registered agent details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on the anniversary of incorporation; a 30-calendar-day grace period applies before late-filing penalties attach
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the unpaid annual fee; continued non-filing for the statutory period triggers administrative strike-off under the International Companies Act 1987 and forfeiture of company assets to the Government of Samoa

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual government renewal fee for the International Company license (tiered by authorized share capital; base tier reflected here)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on or before each anniversary of incorporation; renewal window runs with the annual-return grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid fee attracts a 10% surcharge and accruing arrears; failure to renew within the prescribed period subjects the IC to administrative strike-off, restoration fees equal to arrears plus penalties, and suspension of tax-exempt status during the default period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual economic substance notification declaring relevant-activity status, Samoa tax residence, and compliance with the Economic Substance Regulations 2019
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, in coordination with the Samoa Commissioner of Inland Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the IC's financial year (e.g., for a 31 December year-end, filing due by 31 December of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalties for late or false notification under the Economic Substance Regulations 2019; sustained non-compliance may result in information exchange with the OECD Global Forum and administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is required for a general International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 (s 115); mandatory audit applies only to ICs licensed as international banks under the International Banking Act 2005, international insurers or captives under the International Insurance Act 2005, or where the Registrar or the Samoa International Financial Services Authority imposes an audit under AML/CFT supervision for high-risk client structures such as Class III medical-device manufacturing treasury and financing flows. Audit remains otherwise voluntary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory local GAAP applies to tax-exempt International Companies; annual accounts, when prepared, are generated under IFRS or IFRS for SMEs and are not filed with the Registry; the IC must maintain accounting records sufficient to explain transactions and financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed Samoan Registered Agent maintains a closed beneficial-ownership register and, at each annual renewal, obtains a written UBO confirmation and updated shareholding schedule from the directors; any share transfer is recorded in the Register of Members upon lodgment of the transfer instrument, and the UBO register must be amended within 30 days of the notifiable change; the closed register is not filed publicly but is disclosed to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit upon lawful request.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 – USD 1,500 per annum (licensed registered agent, registered office, annual return preparation, and UBO administration)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 6,000 per annum (voluntary certified audit of a non-public International Company with IP-holding and treasury accounts)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (statutory CIT rate for non-trading/passive-holding companies in Samoa; reduced to 25% for active trading and manufacturing companies under the Income Tax Act 1974 as amended). A Samoa International Company ('IC') registered under the International Companies Act 1987 is excluded from the CIT base: taxable income is deemed nil, producing a 0% effective rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective Samoan corporate tax for the IC. Statutory exemption from income tax, capital gains tax, withholding tax on dividends/interest/royalties, and stamp duty for a period of 20 years from registration (generally renewable/continuing while the IC remains in the Register), subject to the offshore-only conduct condition and current economic substance requirements. A Certificate of Tax Exemption is issued by the Ministry of Revenue through the licensed registered agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form CIR-103 — Company Income Tax Return (Samoa Ministry of Revenue, Inland Revenue Division; electronic filing through the MoR e-Tax Online Portal at www.revenue.gov.ws). For a tax-exempt International Company, the operative filing is the IC Annual Return/Declaration of Exemption filed through the licensed registered agent with the Registrar of International Companies & Financial Services Providers, with reference no. IC-AR.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Non-exempt companies pay provisional income tax in four quarterly installments (31 March, 30 June, 30 September, 31 December) with a final year-end return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed within six months after the end of the company's tax year; for a 31 December year-end, filing is due by 30 June of the following year. The IC Annual Return to the Registrar is due by the anniversary date of registration (or the 31 December of the year, as directed), failing which annual fees are doubled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), registered office, and name/licence number of the registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Samoa IC registration number and the licensed agent's details; attach the Certificate of Tax Exemption and the Certificate of Good Standing for the filing year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax year start and end dates, and confirmation of the accounting standard applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the IC has a non-calendar fiscal year, attach the director's resolution adopting it; no Ministerial approval is required for an IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from business, dividends, interest, royalties, and other non-exempt income sourced in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: IC: enter 0 if all income is offshore-derived; disclose any 'relevant activity' income in the ESR annex (for exemption status monitoring), not in the CIT gross income box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income, identified by statutory provision.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Write 'International Companies Act 1987, s.12 — taxable income deemed nil'; do not claim exemptions under the domestic Income Tax Act that are unavailable to non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions (cost of goods, opex, depreciation, interest, and IP amortization).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax-exempt IC: leave nil. If taxable onshore income exists, claim only arm's-length expenses supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (Box 3 minus Box 4 and Box 5).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: enter 0.00. A non-zero entry converts the entity into an onshore taxpayer and forfeits the IC exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on taxable income at the applicable rate (25% for manufacturing/trading; 27% otherwise).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: enter 0.00. Do not self-assess at treaty rates because no comprehensive double taxation agreement applies to Samoa-sourced IC income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and provisional tax paid: foreign tax credits, provisional installments, and other credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: IC: enter 0.00; refunds are not claimable by an entity with nil liability. A non-exempt corporate filer must attach Form CIT-WHT to substantiate any credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: enter 0.00 and pay no balance. Any refund claim from an IC is a red flag triggering a full audit of the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by the director and the registered agent certifying truthfulness and completeness.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Signature by a named natural-person director is mandatory; electronic signature of the licensed agent is accepted by the Registrar but not by the MoR for CIT purposes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty of 10% of the tax assessed (minimum WST 200) plus monthly arrears interest at 1.5%, compounding; late IC annual filing: doubling of the government renewal fee, daily late penalty, and strike-off after continued default. Fraudulent or false filings: fine up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for the responsible director; additionally, the Registrar may deregister the IC and the licensed agent may be civilly liable under the AML/CFT Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IC Annual Return and Declaration of Tax Exemption (IC-AR), filed with the Samoa Registrar of International Companies & Financial Services Providers through the licensed Samoan registered agent (Companies Online Registry e-portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, synchronized with the government renewal fee cycle.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by the registration anniversary date (typically 31 December for calendar-year renewals); a grace period is available only when the territory is under a declared force majeure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IC name, registration number, date of incorporation, and authorized share capital.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact authorized capital because the exemption-zone renewal fee is capital-graded; misstatement is a criminal offence under the International Companies Act 1987.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office and registered agent confirmation (license number, address in Apia).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cannot be a PO Box of the agent; a physical street address in Samoa is required, and the agent must accept service of process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and officers (names, addresses, nationality, and date of appointment).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; at least one director must be a natural person; nominee arrangements must be disclosed to the agent for BO record purposes.
Bearer shares are prohibited; BO data must be current and retrievable by the Financial Intelligence Unit under the AML/CFT Act 2018.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax exemption declaration — confirm no revenue derived from business with Samoan residents and no Samoan land/property interests.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the operative attestation for the 0% CIT rate. Any false declaration triggers retrospective taxation at 25%/27% plus penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-renewal or late annual return: automatic administrative strike-off, ICP registration fee arrears with penalty at 10% of fees, forfeiture of the company name, and in default of three consecutive periods, dissolution; directors have personal obligation to settle fees when the IC has no assets, and restoration of a struck-off IC is by court order in the Supreme Court of Samoa.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% final non-resident withholding tax on dividends paid by a Samoan domestic company. Dividends and distributions declared by a Samoan International Company are wholly exempt from Samoan tax: the IC regime imposes no dividend withholding, and the effective repatriation rate is 0% in Samoa (foreign tax applies exclusively in the shareholder's residence jurisdiction).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network of practical relevance for dividend relief; its Pacific instruments (including with New Zealand and Australia) are predominantly tax information exchange agreements (TIEAs), not rate-limiting DTAs. Protocol to invoke relief: (1) verify the shareholder's residence jurisdiction and confirm whether a comprehensive DTA exists — none reduces the Samoan statutory 15% rate; (2) obtain from the MoR a Certificate of Tax Exemption for the IC together with a Certificate of Residence/Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), signed by the Commissioner, validating 0% Samoan tax status; (3) submit the TRC and IC Certificate of Good Standing to the foreign revenue authority for foreign tax credit or participation exemption, evidencing that no Samoan WHT or CIT has been borne; (4) where the foreign jurisdiction applies CFC rules, provide the IC registers and ESR file to rebut a substance challenge. All claims must be renewed annually.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Samoan WHT on non-residents: interest 15%, royalties 15% (Income Tax Act 1974 as amended; no DTA reduction available). For an IC, royalty and interest payments to non-residents (e.g., stent IP license fees paid by the operating subsidiary to the IC, or interest on shareholder loans) are exempt from Samoan WHT under the International Companies Act 1987, provided the recipient does not have a business presence in Samoa and the underlying funds are not derived from onshore business. Interest paid by the IC to a Samoan-resident lender, however, would be caught by the domestic 15% WHT and is a red flag for loss of offshore character.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa has not enacted a formal Local File/Master File statutory threshold in its Income Tax Act; the MoR may, however, apply the arm's-length standard and adjust any associated-enterprise transaction under the general anti-avoidance and recharacterization provisions. Prudent compliance threshold for the IC: prepare and retain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (master file, local file, and country-by-country indicators where applicable) whenever cross-border related-party flows attributable to the Samoa IC exceed WST 1,000,000 (approximately USD 380,000) per annum, or when the IC holds material intangible property (stent patents, trademarks, or regulatory approvals). Where the group is headed by or includes entities in jurisdictions applying BEPS Action 13 thresholds (e.g., EUR 750 million consolidated revenue for CbCR; EUR 50 million for Master File; EUR 3 million related-party sales for Local File), those thresholds bind the group and the Samoa entity must be covered.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable. Samoa applies Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) to International Companies carrying on 'relevant activities', including banking, financing, leasing, headquarters, shipping, holding-pure-equity, and intellectual property holding. A Samoa IC holding coronary drug-eluting stent IP (patents and regulatory dossiers) and receiving royalties or service income must demonstrate all of the following in Samoa: (a) direction and management (board meetings physically held in Samoa, minutes kept at the registered office); (b) adequate premises and equipment; (c) adequate qualified full-time employees in Samoa; (d) adequate annual operating expenditure in Samoa proportionate to income; and (e) core income-generating activities (DEMPE functions: development, enhancement, maintenance, protection, and exploitation of the IP) performed in Samoa. A pure IP-holding company is subject to enhanced substance scrutiny and a rebuttable presumption that its income requires substantial local DEMPE activity; failure leads to information exchange with the beneficial owner's tax administration, penalties, and strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion — Abuse of IC Tax-Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the drug-eluting stent manufacturing and IP-licensing business from a Hong Kong or Singapore office while filing nil Samoan returns, holding board meetings outside Samoa, and using the IC as a pure booking center without any Samoan DEMPE activity, employees, premises, or expenditure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retrospective withdrawal of the tax exemption; reassessment of CIT at 25%/27% on all income since exemption commencement; late-payment interest at 1.5% per month and penalties up to 100% of the under-assessed tax; mandatory automatic exchange of information (Global Forum, CRS/AEOI) leading to foreign assessments; deregistration of the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the licensed registered agent are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid taxes where the IC is struck off while liabilities remain; personal fines up to WST 100,000; imprisonment up to 5 years for knowingly authorizing false nil returns; travel bans and director disqualification orders available under Samoan company and tax administration law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Economic Substance Failure — Shell Company / Harmful IP Regime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC holds high-value stent IP and books large royalty streams but performs no DEMPE functions in Samoa; substance is only paper-thin (no payroll, no physical board room); failure to file the ESR annual report or making a false ESR declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalty of up to WST 150,000 per relevant activity for false ESR declarations; deregistration by the Registrar; adverse EU/OECD listing consequential countermeasures (refusals of deductions, withholding tax sanctions in EU jurisdictions); exchange of information with the beneficial owner's jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false ESR declarations face criminal fines and imprisonment of up to 7 years; disqualification from managing any company in Samoa; the registered agent loses its licence and may be sued in negligence by affected shareholders; foreign courts may impose personal liability for the foreign tax consequences triggered by the sham substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Breach — High-Risk Class III Medical Trade Corridor
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the letter-of-credit/SWIFT corridors for stent export transactions without current beneficial ownership records; undisclosed nominee shareholders; invoicing through the IC to circumvent sanctions in the destination healthcare market; cash or third-party settlement of payments without economic justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fines up to WST 1,000,000; asset freezing orders; revocation of the registered agent's licence; mandatory suspicious transaction reporting to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit; blacklisting of the IC under the high-risk medical-device trade typology; debanking by correspondent banks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally indictable with imprisonment up to 14 years; personal confiscation of proceeds of crime; travel bans and extradition exposure under mutual legal assistance treaties; statutory duty of the registered agent to report directors who tolerate anonymous beneficiaries.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Misrepresentation to Revenue Authorities — False Exemption Certification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing the IC Annual Return claiming zero onshore activity while simultaneously claiming manufacturing-related losses, tax credits, or refunds in the foreign parent's jurisdiction; submitting a Certificate of Tax Exemption to the foreign tax authority as evidence of 'tax clearance' for Class III medical device approvals; double-dipping on foreign tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: MoR audit and revocation of the exemption certificate; penalty equal to 200% of avoided tax; criminal fine up to WST 500,000; notification of the foreign tax authority through exchange of information; cancellation of the IC registration and the registered agent's consent to continue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal restitution orders for taxes evaded; imprisonment up to 10 years for false certification; travel bans; in cross-border insolvency, a court may pierce the corporate veil and hold the ultimate controlling shareholders personally liable for misrepresentations to tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Regulatory Fatal Red Flag — Unauthorized Class III Medical Device Marketing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Marketing the Samoa IC's tax-exempt status as a substitute for FDA, CE, TGA, or WHO premarket approval of the coronary drug-eluting stent; manufacturing and exporting Class III devices outside of an ISO 13485 quality system or the destination market's marketing authorization; making fraudulent statements of biocompatibility and clinical performance in letters of credit documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Seizure and destruction of product at ports of entry; criminal product-liability sanctions in the destination jurisdiction; revocation of the Samoan IC and its registered agent; loss of DTA/exemption benefits if the regulating authority reports the fraud to the MoR or the Samoa FIU.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are exposed to personal product-liability judgments, extradition requests, and imprisonment in the destination jurisdiction; personal fines for export trade fraud; disqualification from future medical device trades; the corporate veil is pierced in most common-law destination jurisdictions for personal injury caused by a fake or mislabeled life-saving device.
